# INFO — Rob Wigboldus Vishandel

Research dossier for the landing page build. Everything here was gathered from
publicly available sources on **2026-09-04**. Each fact carries a confidence
level; only **High** and **Medium** facts may appear on the website, and only in
the wording allowed under "Copy rules" at the bottom.

---

## 1. Identity

| Field | Value | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Name (Dutch) | Rob Wigboldus Vishandel | High |
| Name (English listings) | Rob Wigboldus Fishmonger | High |
| Type | Fishmonger / herring stand — takeaway counter with a few seats | High |
| Address | Zoutsteeg 6, 1012 LX Amsterdam, Netherlands | High |
| Phone | +31 20 626 3388 | High |
| Official website | **None** — this is the reason the project exists | High |
| Facebook | facebook.com/profile.php?id=147953155400492 | High |
| Instagram | [@robwigboldusvishandel](https://www.instagram.com/robwigboldusvishandel/) — ~116 followers, last posts 2021, effectively dormant | High |

The business has no owned web presence beyond two low-activity social profiles.
Its entire online footprint is third-party: review aggregators, travel guides,
and food blogs. The landing page is therefore the **first canonical source of
truth** about the shop, which raises the bar on factual accuracy.

---

## 2. Location and setting

- **Zoutsteeg** is a narrow pedestrian alley in Amsterdam Centrum connecting
  Nieuwendijk and Damrak, a short walk from **Dam Square**. (High)
- "Zoutsteeg" translates to **Salt Alley**. The name is a genuine Amsterdam
  toponym and is safe to use as a piece of atmosphere. (High)
- Nearest transit landmark cited by listings: **Rokin** metro/tram. (Medium)
- The shop is repeatedly described as **hidden / easy to miss** — reviewers find
  it "tucked away," "off the main paths," "in a tiny passageway." (High)
- **Very small**: roughly three small tables plus a bar top facing the street;
  seats somewhere around 7–10 people. Most trade is standing/takeaway. (Medium)

> The "hidden alley" quality is the single strongest narrative hook available.
> It is corroborated across many independent reviews and is not a claim about
> quality, so it carries no factual risk.

---

## 3. What they sell

Corroborated across multiple independent listings and reviews:

| Item (Dutch) | English gloss | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Broodje haring | Herring on a soft roll, with raw onion and pickle | High |
| Haring / maatjesharing | Salt-cured raw herring, served whole | High |
| Kibbeling | Battered, deep-fried cod pieces | High |
| Gerookte paling | Smoked eel | Medium |
| Gerookte zalm | Smoked salmon | Medium |
| Makreel | Mackerel | Medium |
| Broodje kibbeling / gebakken vis | Fried fish on a roll | Medium |

Additional detail:

- The **broodje haring is the signature item** — it dominates reviews and is what
  people travel to the alley for. (High)
- Customers can **choose between several kinds of bread/rolls** for the sandwich. (Medium)
- Standard Dutch garnish: **raw white onion and sweet-sour pickle**. (High)
- Fish is sold both **as a snack to eat there** and **as raw fish over the
  counter** — it is a working fishmonger, not only a snack bar. (Medium)

### Pricing — do not publish

Reported figures are inconsistent and drawn from reviews spanning several years
(sandwich ~€3 in an older review; kibbeling ~€5; hake ~€6; "€1–€10 per person"
in one aggregator). Prices change and none of these come from the business.

**Decision: no prices anywhere on the site.** Describe the shop as
affordable/everyday in tone only if needed, without numbers.

---

## 4. Hours

Sources conflict. Listed in order of authority:

| Source | Hours | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Instagram bio (**first-party**) | Open 7 days a week, **09:00–18:00** | Profile is dormant since 2021 |
| Google / Wanderlog / RestaurantGuru | Daily **08:00–17:00** | Aggregated, unverified |
| Several travel listings | Daily 8 AM – 5 PM | Echo of the above |

**Decision:** publish the **first-party Instagram hours (daily 09:00–18:00)**,
because they are the only figures the business itself has stated. Add a short,
honest line inviting visitors to call ahead, and flag hours as the number-one
item for the owner to confirm before the site goes live.

Do **not** invent seasonal hours, holiday closures, or a kitchen-closing time.

---

## 5. Payment

Multiple independent listings state **cash only** (a few soften this to "cash
preferred; card not always accepted"). Reviews are consistent with cash.

**Decision:** surface this prominently but neutrally — it is genuinely useful
information for a visitor standing in an alley, and getting it wrong is worse
than omitting it. Wording: *"Cash is the safest bet — bring some with you."*
This is true under either reading of the sources. Flag for owner confirmation.

---

## 6. Reputation and social proof

| Platform | Rating | Volume | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google | 4.6 / 5 | ~1,700+ reviews | High |
| TripAdvisor | 4.7 / 5 | ~861 reviews | High |
| Foursquare | 8.8 / 10 | ~61 reviews | Medium |

Category rankings are reported inconsistently (one source says #14 of 4,717
Amsterdam restaurants, another #9 of 1,894 seafood restaurants). **Do not
publish any ranking claim.** Ratings and review counts are safe; round them
down and attribute them ("4.6 on Google, from over 1,600 reviews").

### Verbatim review quotes (safe to use, attributed as visitor reviews)

- "One of the nicest herring in the city. The fish he uses is really fresh and
  slightly fatty so it's very delicious compared to other stalls."
- "Small shop in the alley. Can seat about 7–10 people. Perfect for breakfast.
  Uncle who owns the shop is very very nice."
- "I went to this cosy restaurant just to try a real herring. The owner was so
  friendly and warm-welcoming and the herring itself was really delicious."
- "The best tasting herring in the city. It is also the cheapest one I found."
- "Tucked away, good herring sandwich."

Use quotes **verbatim**, marked as visitor reviews, without invented names,
photos, or dates. Do not fabricate testimonials.

### Recurring themes

Positive: freshness of the fish; the owner serving personally; value; the
find-it-yourself alley location; speed.

Negative: a minority of reviews describe service as **brusque or rude**, and a
few find the herring comparable to other stalls. This is normal for a
high-volume counter. It is not something the site should address, but it means
the copy must **not** overclaim on hospitality — no "warmest welcome in
Amsterdam." Let the quotes speak instead.

---

## 7. Photography

There is **no first-party photography available under any usable licence**. The
Instagram account is dormant with a handful of posts; review-site photos belong
to their uploaders.

**Decision (confirmed with the user):** curated free-licence stock — herring and
North Sea fish, Dutch counter/market detail, narrow Amsterdam alleys and canal
houses. Images are downloaded into `assets/img/` so the page works offline from
`file://`, and every file is credited in `assets/img/CREDITS.md`.

**Hard rule:** no stock photo may be presented as a picture of this shop, its
staff, or its food. Photos are atmosphere and subject matter only — never
captioned or framed in a way that implies "this is Rob Wigboldus Vishandel."
No stock photo of a person is used as if it were the owner.

## 8. Facts that were found but must NOT be used

| Claim seen in the wild | Why it is excluded |
|---|---|
| "Over four decades in business" / founding year | Traced only to auto-generated aggregator pages. Unverifiable. |
| "Oldest fishmonger in Amsterdam" | No source. |
| "Sashimi-grade herring" | A reviewer's phrasing, not a business claim. |
| "Kesbeke-brand pickles" | Single low-quality source; naming a supplier is a factual claim. |
| Family history, generations, named owner biography | Nothing verifiable beyond reviewers calling the man behind the counter "Rob" / "the uncle." |
| Awards, certifications, sustainability claims | None found. |
| Specific prices | Inconsistent and dated. See §3. |
| TripAdvisor / Google category rankings | Sources contradict each other. |

---

## 9. Audience

Two groups, in this order of volume:

1. **Visitors to Amsterdam** — on a phone, standing near Dam Square, deciding
   in under a minute whether to walk into an alley they cannot see down. They
   need: what this is, is it good, how far, is it open, do I need cash.
2. **Amsterdam locals** — buying fish, or bringing someone visiting. They need:
   what is on the counter today, hours, where exactly.

The page is **mobile-first and location-first**. Design for one-handed use in
daylight, on a slow connection, in a hurry.

---

## 10. Copy rules for the build

1. Never state a fact this document marks Low confidence or lists in §8.
2. No prices. No founding year. No ranking claims. No invented history.
3. Ratings and review counts must be attributed to the platform and rounded down.
4. Review quotes verbatim, marked as visitor reviews, unattributed to individuals.
5. Dutch product names lead; short English glosses follow. Body copy is English.
6. Hours and cash-only are presented as "confirm by phone" facts, not guarantees.
7. Stock photography is never framed as depicting this business (see §7).
8. Tone: plain, specific, a little dry. The shop is a counter in an alley that
   sells very good herring. That is already a good story — do not inflate it.
